source_review.notes: Checked seven official or primary sources. RFC 1034 defines DNS concepts, distributed resource data, and resolvers. RFC 2782 defines SRV service location with priority, weight, port, and protocol-specific usage requirements. RFC 9460 defines SVCB/HTTPS service binding and parameters. Current Kubernetes documentation describes service/pod DNS and EndpointSlices. Current gRPC documentation describes DNS/xDS/custom target resolution feeding client behavior. Current Envoy documentation describes xDS dynamic resources and management-server discovery. Ecosystem mechanisms are examples; local identity, consistency, health, failover, and routing policy remain explicit design decisions.

evidence: Checked registered G_t, lease-valid L_t, health H_t, identity I_t, policy P_t(q), true eligible set E_t(q), and delayed local view E-hat_t(q).
Checked positive weights w_i, normalized probabilities p_i, lease renewal/length/expiry, revision v, and age a.
Confirmed eligibility is an intersection and weighted denominators range over the currently eligible set.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Health and weights are scoped claims; neither changes nonnegotiable identity, tenant, version, residency, shard, or consistency predicates.

evidence: Recomputed weights 2,3,5 with sum 10 as 20%,30%,50%.
Recomputed remaining weights 2,3 with sum 5 as 40%,60% after weight-5 endpoint drains.
Checked 30-second TTL versus 30-minute connection-pool example and 5% canary scenario for dimensional consistency.
Confirmed all ten worked examples and five exercise/answer pairs are distinct.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Endpoint counts, TTLs, connection ages, canary share, and weights are scenarios rather than production measurements.

evidence: Verified an endpoint absent from any G/L/H/I/P set cannot belong to their intersection.
Constructed endpoint failure immediately after discovery response, disproving discovery as a guarantee of current reachability.
Constructed address reuse plus delayed delete and verified generation equality prevents deletion of the replacement lease.
Verified normalized eligible weights sum to one before and after membership change.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Local views are necessarily delayed; connection identity, deadlines, passive evidence, and bounded stale policy handle that limitation.

evidence: Reviewed DNS/SRV/SVCB, registry/watch, snapshots/deltas, client/proxy/hybrid routing, orchestrator registration, leases, generation fencing, and long-lived pools.

Reviewed liveness/readiness/serving/draining, active/passive health, operation-specific eligibility, weighted/least-load/power-of-two/hash/priority/locality algorithms, affinity, shards, leaders, and causal reads.
Reviewed forged registration, SSRF/poisoning, wrong identity/tenant/environment/region/version, stale/malformed/partial updates, split brain, negative cache, empty sets, and control-plane outage.
Reviewed ejection cascades, overload, retry storms, rolling versions, zone/region loss, data residency/freshness, failback, clock/pause, compaction, recovery, and telemetry cardinality/privacy.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Coverage spans naming, trust, membership, time, health, consistency, selection, load, security, control plane, geography, observation, and recovery.

evidence: Confirmed logical service identity is stable while endpoint addresses/generations remain ephemeral and authenticated independently.
Confirmed registration/lease/readiness/drain/update/cache semantics have authoritative sources, bounded age, revision, and last-known-good behavior.
Confirmed routing chooses only policy-compatible eligible endpoints and services still verify workload identity, authorization, shard epoch, consistency, and effects.
Confirmed retries/ejection/failover are bounded, capacity-aware, nonnegotiable policy preserving, observable, progressively operated, and recovery-tested.
invariant_checking.notes: An empty safe set produces explicit unavailable/bounded wait, never a hardcoded or policy-relaxed endpoint fallback.

evidence: Reviewed eligibility conjunction and confirmed each predicate independently excludes unsafe endpoints.
Reviewed staleness impossibility and confirmed no snapshot can guarantee endpoint reachability after observation.
Reviewed generation fencing and confirmed a stale generation cannot delete a current lease when compare-and-delete is enforced.
Reviewed weight normalization and confirmed results while noting eligibility/weight semantics as prerequisites.
proof_review.notes: Logical proofs bound the design; actual resolver/runtime cache, endpoint, capacity, and failure behavior require empirical verification.

evidence: Confirmed formal passages are labeled eligibility conjunction, staleness impossibility, generation-fencing argument, and weight normalization.
Confirmed DNS/SRV/SVCB, Kubernetes, gRPC, and xDS claims remain scoped to cited standards/ecosystems.
Confirmed service identity, metadata, lease, health, cache, routing, failover, security, observability, and recovery choices are architectural policy rather than universal protocol mandates.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Standards mechanisms, ecosystem behavior, logical consequences, and local operating policy remain separate.

evidence: All seven official or primary references were checked on 2026-09-02 where current documentation applies.

The chapter requires actual cache/TTL/pool behavior, revisions/convergence, endpoint identity/readiness, routing distributions, saturation/ejection, fault/load tests, failover state/residency/capacity, and recovery evidence.
No real discovery system's freshness, availability, endpoint count, load distribution, security, failover, capacity, convergence, or recovery readiness is asserted.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Worked examples illustrate mechanism and evidence interpretation but cannot establish a deployed system's safety.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed identity/mechanism selection, client-versus-server routing, registration/leases/fencing, health/drain, snapshots/deltas, caches, eligibility, algorithms, capacity/overload, retries/circuits/pools, consistency/affinity/version, security, locality/failover, observability, testing, and recovery as one discovery-routing discipline.

practitioner_review.notes: Checked implementability through controller-authenticated registrations, server-time leases/generations, readiness/drain sequencing, versioned snapshots/deltas with ACK/NACK, bounded caches and negative answers, explicit filters/empty behavior, weighted/locality/shard policies, endpoint identity validation, retry/ejection caps, causal routing, multi-region gates, convergence telemetry, and fault/restore rehearsals.

pedagogical_review.notes: The module separates stable names from ephemeral endpoints and resolver from router, then develops membership, time, health, policy, algorithms, consistency, trust, failover, and operation. Counterexamples expose registration, health, TTL, least-load, nearest-endpoint, and discovery-authority shortcuts. Ten examples and five integrative exercises have complete answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external standards-body, platform vendor, network, security, distributed-systems, or practitioner review is claimed.
